problem: Fixed-camera construction site monitoring cannot adapt when line-of-sight obstacles occlude workers, so object detection of workers fails under occlusion.
motivation: Reliable worker monitoring matters for construction safety, but static cameras cannot reposition to see occluded workers. A mobile robot that actively navigates to different viewing angles of a single worker could overcome occlusion.
key_idea: Use a mobile robot with deep-reinforcement-learning-based object-goal navigation to move to viewpoints around a single worker so the detector can see the worker despite occlusion.
insight: Only the abstract is available, so no ablation evidence is visible. The abstract claims that active viewpoint navigation gives better path efficiency and proactive monitoring than rule-based and fixed-camera baselines in occluded scenes.
method: State-action-reward design: the paper designs the RL state, action and reward structure for occlusion-aware worker-centered navigation.
Deep RL path planning policy: a navigation policy is learned with deep reinforcement learning to reach various viewing angles of one worker.
Object-goal navigation with mobile robot: the robot navigates toward the worker target and uses object detection for monitoring.
Validation: the learned policy is compared with a rule-based approach and a fixed-camera system.

setting.backbone: deep RL policy (details not given in abstract) plus an object detection model
setting.training_data: not specified in abstract (RL training, likely in simulation)

results: The abstract reports improved path efficiency and proactive monitoring in occluded environments versus rule-based and fixed-camera baselines, but gives no quantitative numbers.
limitations: Abstract only; no quantitative evaluation or benchmark is reported.
Focuses on a single worker; multi-worker scenarios are not addressed in the abstract.
